To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the multi-fidelity Gaussian processes can be a better choice for asymmetric problems, the multi-task Gaussian processes are a better choice for symmetric problems, and the performance of MOGPs depends on the problem settings, such as the number of training data, the correlation among outputs, and the number of outputs.

the multi-output Gaussian process (MOGP) models can be classified into two categories, namely symmetric and asymmetric models, and that the performance of MOGPs can be improved by choosing the right model for the right application.

(1) for symmetric MOGPs, the separable covariance function and joint hyperparameter inference are preferred, while the non-separable covariance function and separate hyperparameter inference are recommended for asymmetric MOGPs; (2) the integrated modeling strategy is preferred over the decomposed modeling strategy for both symmetric and asymmetric scenarios, and (3) the information transfer between outputs is bidirectional for both symmetric and asymmetry scenarios.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of MOGPs that can improve the prediction quality for multi-output regression problems.
a comprehensive review of the state-of-the art MOGPs and their applications in multi-output regression problems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the multi-output regression problems with heterotopic training data, the symmetric MOGPs can achieve better predictions than the asymmetric MOGPs in most cases, and for the isotopic training data, it is still not clear whether the symmetric MOGPS can outperform the asymmetric MOGPS.

, for symmetric problems, we should use the MOGPs with non-separable covariance functions and the integrated modeling process, and for asymmetric problems, the MOGPs that transfer useful information from related low fidelity output(s) to high fidelity output(s) are preferred.

, in symmetric scenarios, the multi-task Gaussian processes (MTGP) and the multi-kernel Gaussian processes (MKGP) are more suitable for isotopic data, while the multi-task Gaussian process with low rank approximation (MTGPLR) is better for heterotopic data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MOGPs with the bidirectional information transfer and the non-separable covariance function are more promising for multi-output regression problems.

MOGPs are powerful tools to improve the predictions of multi-output regression problems, especially in the cases with high correlations and small training data, but their performances are highly problem-dependent.
the symmetric MOGPs are more suitable to deal with heterotopic and small training datasets, while the asymmetric MOGPs are suitable to handle isotopic and large training datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for multi-output regression problems, the symmetric and asymmetric MOGPs can be used in different situations, and their performance is sensitive to the training data and hyperparameters, and can be further improved.
